correctness.rationale: For an edge uv, triangle inequality forces |d(w,u)-d(w,v)|<=1. Thus local resolution, defined by unequal distances, is equivalent to distance difference one. That equality is exactly the geodesic condition for strong resolution of an adjacent pair, in either direction. Therefore L_S(u,v)=L(u,v) edge by edge, making the two feasible function classes identical. The finite checker directly confirms this for all connected labeled graphs on 2..6 vertices and verifies C4 as a value-one counterexample to the path-only claim.

evidence: The 2018 source defines local resolving neighborhoods by unequal distances and proves ldim_f(G)=1 exactly for bipartite graphs; its published version lists MSC 05C12.
The 2021 source defines local strong resolving neighborhoods on adjacent pairs by the geodesic strong-resolution condition, states ldim_f(G)<=lsdim_f(G), and asserts lsdim_f(G)=1 exactly for paths.
The 2023 source repeats the local-strong definition and reports value one for even cycles, consistent with the new universal equality.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier and later sources do not dominate the claim: they retain the parameters as separate notions. Comparing the definitions on a single adjacent pair yields the universal identity and exposes the path-only statement as incompatible with the definitions.

value.rationale: The theorem collapses an entire separately introduced fractional invariant to an existing parameter on every connected graph. It identifies the feasible polytopes, not just their minima, so all optimizer structure and all previous LFMD theorems transfer immediately. It also corrects the basic value-one classification under the published LFSMD definition. This is a structural simplification of the theory rather than a family-specific computation.
